comparisons.what: Compare the partially coherent aerial images computed independently using the Abbe and Hopkins formulations to verify that they agree.
Compare the optimized free-form source next to the best parametric source.
Compare the oscillation of the CD change of the isolated line as its neighbour moves away with the mutual coherence function.

constraints: Exposure is fixed at wavelength 193.368 nm through water (refractive index 1.436) with a projection lens of NA 1.35.
The mask is held fixed as a thin 6% attenuated phase-shift mask where dark regions transmit amplitude sqrt(0.06) with a phase of pi using the Kirchhoff thin-mask approximation.
Imaging must be scalar with no polarization.
The paper must state plainly that imaging is scalar and what that changes at NA 1.35, specifically that it overstates contrast and depth of focus.
The partially coherent aerial image must be computed two independent ways (Abbe and Hopkins) that must agree.
Patterns are constrained to vertical lines (dark on the attenuated mask) and spaces with a target line width of 40 nm.
Resist imaging is constrained to a constant-threshold aerial image with no resist blur.
Dose must be anchored so the densest pitch prints at 40 nm at best focus.
A one-dimensional OPC must set the mask line width at every pitch so it prints at 40 nm at best focus.
The process window tolerance requires a CD tolerance of +/-10% of 40 nm at 5% exposure latitude.
The free-form pixelated source optimization must keep mirror symmetry.
A long run is allowed (source optimization may take hours), and the runtime must be reported.
Every number must be reported with its numerical error (grid, source sampling, focus step) and it must be stated when a result is only a check of the code.
The implementation must use Python with numpy and scipy, and matplotlib with the Agg backend.
The study must produce a paper that answers the question with numbers.
Only sources that have actually been found and read may be cited, and unconfirmed references must be stated as such rather than cited.
